issues.display_title: Issue #4077: Add Bottom Pagination Controls to Google Portfolio Grid
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A UX friction point has been identified on the "Google Portfolio" page. Currently, the pagination controls (page numbers to navigate to the next/previous page) are only located at the top of the tour grid.

When a user changes their view settings to display a large number of tours per page (e.g., 24 or 36 items), they scroll down to view them. Once they reach the bottom of the list, they are forced to scroll all the way back to the top just to click the "Next Page" button.

To improve navigation flow, we need to duplicate the existing top pagination component and place it at the bottom of the grid as well.

Sub-tasks

  • Component Duplication: Re-use the existing pagination component that currently sits at the top of the list.
  • UI Placement: Render a second instance of this pagination component at the very bottom of the tour grid container (below the last row of tour cards).
  • State Synchronization: Ensure that both the top and bottom pagination components share the same state. Clicking "Page 2" on the bottom component must correctly update the list and reflect the active state on both paginators.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Pagination numbers/controls are clearly visible at both the top and the bottom of the Google Portfolio tour grid.
  2. Users can successfully navigate to different pages using the new bottom pagination controls.
  3. The UI layout remains clean and the new bottom paginator does not overlap with the chat widget or footer elements.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Logged in to an account that has enough Google Portfolio tours to produce multiple pages at higher page sizes (24 / 36 per page).
  • Open the Google Portfolio page.

Scenario 1 — Bottom paginator visible

  1. Set "tours per page" to 24 (then repeat with 36).
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the tour grid.
  3. ✅ Expected: A pagination control (same as the top one) is visible at the bottom, below the last row of tour cards.

Scenario 2 — Navigate using bottom controls

  1. At the bottom paginator, click "Next Page" / "Page 2".
  2. ✅ Expected: The grid loads the correct next page of tours.

Scenario 3 — State synchronization (both paginators in sync)

  1. Click Page 2 on the bottom paginator.
  2. Scroll to the top.
  3. ✅ Expected: The top paginator also shows Page 2 as active. (And vice versa: changing the page from the top updates the bottom.)

Scenario 4 — Consistency across page sizes

  1. Change page size (12 → 24 → 36) and navigate using the bottom controls each time.
  2. ✅ Expected: Both paginators always reflect the same current page and the correct total page count for the selected page size.

Scenario 5 — Layout / no overlap

  1. With the bottom paginator showing, inspect the area near the bottom-right chat widget and the footer (Terms / Privacy / © GoThru).
  2. ✅ Expected: The bottom paginator does not overlap or get hidden behind the chat widget or footer; layout stays clean on desktop and at smaller/responsive widths.

Scenario 6 — Single page edge case

  1. Set a page size large enough that all tours fit on one page.
  2. ✅ Expected: Pagination behaves sensibly (no broken/duplicate controls; consistent with the top paginator's behavior).

Pass criteria: All scenarios behave as the ✅ Expected results, top and bottom paginators stay perfectly in sync, and the new control never overlaps the chat widget or footer.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §4 (Portfolio & custom filters).

issues.display_title: Issue #4085: Integrate API Get Panorama Manual Blur
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Integrate the Get Panorama Manual Blur API into the dashboard's Anonymize 360 Images / Manual Blur flow.

This covers wiring the frontend to the GET endpoint that retrieves existing manual blur data for a panorama (e.g. from the 8_blooring table), so previously saved manual blur regions can be loaded back and displayed/edited in the UI.

Scope

  • Integrate the Get Panorama Manual Blur API endpoint to fetch existing manual blur data for a given panorama.
  • Load and render the retrieved blur regions in the Manual Blur / 360 Image Connector UI.
  • Handle API responses/states correctly (loading, empty/no-blur, success, error).
  • Reflect blur status accurately (e.g. the blue indicator on thumbnails that have manual blur data).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Existing manual blur data for a panorama is successfully fetched via the API.
  2. Retrieved blur regions are correctly displayed in the UI (and available for editing where applicable).

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §4 (Tour editor: face/plate blurring). Companion to #4075 (Integrate API Manual Blur); related to #4073, #4074.

issues.display_title: Issue #4081: Handle Publish Button Stuck on Infinite "Validating..." State
issues.main_description_html:
Description

A bug has been reported on the Publish to Street View flow: after clicking Publish, the button enters a "Validating..." state and spins indefinitely — the validation never resolves to Success or Failure, blocking the user from publishing.

The reporter notes the token/scopes appear OK (valid streetviewpublish, userinfo.email, userinfo.profile, openid scopes), so this is a state-resolution / timeout-handling issue rather than an auth problem — the frontend fails to settle the validation state. Affected users are forced to manually push the tour, which is a problem when clients need it published urgently.

Reference Data

  • Moderation ID: 3559433
  • User ID: 3514
  • Symptom: "Validating..." button never resolves (infinite spinner).

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The validation process must reach a final resolution (Success or Failure) and must not remain stuck spinning indefinitely.
  2. If the validation fails or times out, the UI must display a clear error message, and the button must return to its active state so the user can retry.
  3. The tour can successfully proceed to the publish phase if the validation passes on the backend.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §4 (Publishing: Google Business / Street View Blue Line) and §10 ("Stuck publishing" failure mode).

issues.display_title: Issue #4061: Bug Fix Photographer Main Location Not Saving
issues.main_description_html:
Task Description

Brainstorming File:
2026-06-02-photographer-location-save-fix-design.md

Acceptance Criteria

AC-1: No crash on first visit (no location record)

  • Given a newly submitted user who has never set a main location
  • When the /photographer/location page loads
  • Then executeGetLocation handles a null or missing location field gracefully ? no silent TypeError
  • And the form renders in an empty state (no location on map, search field blank)
  • And hasMainLocation is false

AC-2: No crash when location is 0,0

  • Given the API returns { latitude: 0, longitude: 0 } for a user
  • When the page loads
  • Then the zero-location branch resets state (same behavior as AC-1) without crashing

AC-3: Save + backend persistence confirmed ? happy path

  • Given the user selects a valid location via Google Places
  • When the user clicks the save button
  • And the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 and the GET re-fetch returns the saved coordinates
  • Then a success toast appears
  • And hasMainLocation becomes true
  • And the map and search field reflect the saved location

AC-4: Save returns 200 but backend did not persist ? silent failure detected

  • Given the PATCH API returns HTTP 200 (success toast fires)
  • But the subsequent GET re-fetch returns null or 0,0 (backend did not actually save)
  • Then hasMainLocation is reset to false
  • And the form resets to empty ? the user can see the save did not stick

AC-5: Re-fetch runs automatically after save

  • Given a successful save (PATCH 200)
  • Then executeGetLocation is called immediately after the success toast
  • And hasMainLocation is only set to true by the re-fetch result, not by the save handler directly

AC-6: Save API error handled correctly

  • Given the PATCH API returns a non-200 response
  • Then an error toast shows res.data.details or res.data.messages
  • And executeGetLocation is NOT re-called
  • And hasMainLocation remains unchanged

AC-7: Subsequent visit shows saved location

  • Given a user who successfully saved a location (AC-3 confirmed)
  • When they navigate away and return to /photographer/location
  • Then executeGetLocation loads and displays the saved coordinates and address
  • And hasMainLocation is true

AC-8: Sub-location and existing behavior unchanged

  • Then sub-location save, delete, and load behavior is unaffected
  • And the floppy-disk save button position and appearance are unchanged
  • And onSelectLocation (Google Places selection) and onSetLocationByLatLng (lat/lng input) behave exactly as before
